input.quote: If the Management Committee nevertheless reclaims any capacity in the APCN 2 assigned to such defaulting Party, the defaulting Party shall not be entitled to any payment or credit for the reclaimed capacity. ... The defaulting Party is not entitled to any reimbursement of any amounts it had paid under this Agreement.
input.rationale: There is no express liquidated damages or penalty clause in the Agreement, but Subparagraph 23.2 imposes a forfeiture-style penalty on us: following a payment default (triggered as little as three months after a due date under 23.1), our allocated APCN 2 capacity may be reclaimed with no payment or credit, and we forfeit all amounts previously paid, while remaining liable for unpaid accounts. That uncompensated forfeiture of our capital contribution is a penalty in substance, is uncapped and unrelated to actual loss, and is triggered by a payment default, so it fails the fallback (a sole early-termination fee capped at three months' fees) and sits in walk-away territory. We therefore target the preferred position: the no-credit and no-reimbursement mechanics are conformed and no Party owes liquidated damages or penalties. The separate no-capital-cost-credit point on voluntary withdrawal (Subparagraph 18.5/p0233) is addressed under the termination rule and is not double-flagged here; interest at prime rate under 7.8 is compensatory and unobjectionable.

proposal.summary: Remove the penal forfeiture of reclaimed capacity and of amounts already paid on default, and bar liquidated damages and penalties.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a penalty-style forfeiture of our capacity and of all amounts we have already paid on a payment default, so we have made the reclaimed capacity payable or creditable to us and confirmed that no Party owes liquidated damages or penalties. If a liquidated amount is unavoidable, our fallback is a sole early-termination fee capped at three months' fees.
